payload.title: Public notebooks are hypothesis generators
payload.decision: Treat every public notebook, writeup, score, threshold, blend, artifact, and routing rule as a hypothesis source rather than a trusted project pipeline. Reconstruct any borrowed mechanism from legal inputs, preregister it, run frozen controls and subgroup tests, independently reproduce it, and benchmark hidden-scale runtime before it can affect official state.
payload.rationale: The ROGII public frontier contains overlap-specific shifts, opaque artifacts, unknown-license dependencies, and gates that fail their own OOF checks. The BirdCLEF winning writeup is useful because its mechanism and controls are explicit, but cross-domain transfer still requires independent ROGII evidence.
payload.revisit_trigger: Never waive the evidence-first reconstruction rule during this competition.
